Reproducing Danish, Aronov & Fee (2017) from CRCNS aa-3¶

Paper. Danish HH, Aronov D, Fee MS (2017). Rhythmic syllable-related activity in a songbird motor thalamic nucleus necessary for learned vocalizations. PLoS ONE 12(6): e0169568. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0169568. The claims file (claims/danish-2017.yaml) was written from the version of record (PMC5472270), with the legends of the supporting information.

Data set. CRCNS aa-3, read from the public bucket crcnsarchive under aa-3/live/: Electrophysiology.tar.gz (4,254,324,000 bytes, MD5 0a93b3d4c7c2f98e8d29ffcb91842db4) and Lesion_Experiments.tar.gz (5,134,663,426 bytes, MD5 0d4f55eba659b1e3976c3220663e6e9e), as listed in the data set's checksums.md5. CRCNS data sets are not versioned; the version recorded is unversioned, and these checksums pin what was read. The paper cites the data set without a version, and there is only this one copy (aa-3/live/; there is no aa-3/old/). The two archives are streamed once each (twice for the lesion archive) and reduced as they are read; nothing is written to disk.

What the data set holds. Multiunit recordings in Uva during singing from 3 birds (the paper recorded 5), with the authors' segmentations and labels, and one day of song before and one day after bilateral Uva lesions from 7 birds (the paper's 7 Uva-lesioned birds). There are no control-lesion birds, no directed-song labels in the lesion data, and no sorted single units.

The labels are not described in the data descriptor beyond "syllable name". The data say what they are: letters a to h (Orange150), a to d (b871) and a to f (Uva4) are the motif syllables, "i" occurs at the start of bouts before "a" (introductory notes), and "k" is a sound of about 210 ms that makes up the files the spreadsheets mark as "distance calls" (b871, Uva4). The descriptor says that introductory notes and calls are unselected; in the files, "i" and "k" are selected. Orange150 has no call labels.

Which neural channel. Each recording has a sound channel and three neural channels (5, 6 and 7, or 1, 2 and 3 for Uva4). The paper describes a single electrode, and neither the descriptor nor the files say which channel is the Uva electrode (the plotting script asks the user to choose 1 to 3). The cell below shows, for each bird and channel, the syllable-onset-aligned MUA. The channel used is, for each bird, the one with the largest range of the onset-aligned average (an assumption; stated with the claims that rest on it, which show the other channels too). The analysis files list files for all three channels (ChannelFiles, which the data set's process_recording.m reads as the neural channels), so they do not settle it. One analysis file, Orange150's first day, ran its event detectors (threshold crossings and stimulus detection) on channel 7, the channel chosen here for that bird. The choice uses the syllable modulation that later claims measure; the fig6 section shows the latencies on every channel.

In [4]:
def song_events(bird, exclude_outside=True):
    """Song files of a bird: selected syllables other than introductory notes and calls."""
    out = []
    for ev in uva.events(eph, bird):
        if exclude_outside and any(ev["props"].get(p, False) for p in uva.OUTSIDE_FLAGS):
            continue
        song = ev["sel"] & ~np.isin(ev["title"], ["i", "k", ""])
        if song.sum() >= 3:
            out.append(ev)
    return out


BIRDS = ["Bird_1-b871", "Bird_2-Orange150", "Bird_3-Uva4"]
chan_rows = []

            r = eph["recs"][ev["key"]]

Clock check. Sound and neural channels are separate files per recording, each with its own header. They share a clock if the syllable labels, made on the sound, line up with the neural signal. The cell below decodes song from MUA: within song files, the MUA in 50 ms windows before syllable onsets against the MUA at random times inside bouts, with the true onsets and with the onsets shifted by 0.5 to 2 s.

In [5]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
for bird in BIRDS:
    out = {}
    for shift in [0, 500, 1000, 2000]:
        auc = []
        for ev in song_events(bird):
            m = eph["recs"][ev["key"]]["mua"][CI[bird]]
            song = ev["sel"] & ~np.isin(ev["title"], ["i", "k", ""])
            on = ev["on"][song] + shift
            on = on[(on > 60) & (on < len(m) - 1)]
            if len(on) < 3:
                continue
            pre = np.array([m[int(t) - 40:int(t)].mean() for t in on])
            inb = np.concatenate([np.arange(int(a), int(b)) for a, b, _ in ev["bouts"]])
            inb = inb[(inb > 60) & (inb < len(m))]
            rnd = np.array([m[t - 40:t].mean() for t in rng.choice(inb, len(on))])
            auc.append(np.mean(pre[:, None] > rnd[None, :]))
        out[shift] = np.mean(auc)
    print(bird, "probability that pre-onset MUA exceeds MUA at a random time in a bout; by onset shift (ms):",
          {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in out.items()})

Electrophysiology claims¶

Common choices for this part, each from the claims file or the paper:

  • MUA is the chosen channel of each bird (assumption above), from song files at sites inside Uva (files whose properties mark them above, below or outside Uva are left out).
  • Bouts are vocal segments with gaps of at most 300 ms (Methods, Sound analysis).
  • The shuffled baseline is reading (a) of the claims file header: averages of the same number of windows taken at random times inside bouts (for the bout-offset claim, outside singing), 1000 times; the band is the 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of the shuffles' minima and maxima over the window (-150 to +150 ms here, a standard choice). Reading (b), MUA circularly shifted within each bout, is run for the syllable-onset and offset claims.
  • Values are per bird and then averaged over the 3 birds; the paper averages over 5.
In [6]:
PRE, POST = 150, 150
LAGS = np.arange(-PRE, POST + 1)


def bird_traces(bird, ci=None):
    ci = CI[bird] if ci is None else ci
    return [(ev, eph["recs"][ev["key"]]["mua"][ci]) for ev in song_events(bird)]


def inside_bout_pool(bird, ci=None):
    pool = []
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird, ci):
        t = np.concatenate([np.arange(int(a), int(b)) for a, b, _ in ev["bouts"]])
        t = t[(t >= PRE) & (t < len(m) - POST - 1)]
        if len(t):
            pool.append((m, t))
    return pool


def event_average(bird, times_of, ci=None):
    rows = []
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird, ci):
        a, _ = uva.aligned(m, times_of(ev), PRE, POST)
        rows.append(a)
    A = np.concatenate(rows)
    return A


def circ_shift_band(bird, times_of, n_shuffle, rng, ci=None):
    """Shuffled baseline reading (b): MUA circularly shifted within each bout relative to the
    event times; band of the shuffles' minima and maxima (2.5 and 97.5 percentiles). The windows
    are cut from the shifted bout taken as periodic, so the 150 ms before and after each event
    come from shifted bout activity too (events at a bout's start see the bout's shifted end)."""
    items = []
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird, ci):
        t = times_of(ev)
        for a, b, _ in ev["bouts"]:
            a, b = int(a), int(b)
            sel = t[(t >= a) & (t < b)]
            if len(sel) and a - PRE >= 0 and b + POST < len(m):
                items.append((m[a - PRE:b + POST], sel - a + PRE, b - a))
    mins, maxs, means = [], [], []
    for _ in range(n_shuffle):
        acc = np.zeros(PRE + POST + 1); n = 0
        for seg, tt, L in items:
            core = seg[PRE:PRE + L]
            sh = np.roll(core, rng.integers(L))
            full = np.take(sh, np.arange(-PRE, L + POST), mode="wrap")
            a, ok = uva.aligned(full, tt, PRE, POST)
            acc += a.sum(0); n += len(a)
        avg = acc / n
        means.append(avg.mean()); mins.append(avg.min()); maxs.append(avg.max())
    return float(np.mean(means)), np.percentile(mins, 2.5), np.percentile(maxs, 97.5)


AVG = {}  # (event name, bird, shuffle) -> (average, level, band low, band high), for the figure


def latency_table(times_of, direction, n_shuffle=1000, seed=0, readings=("a",), ci_of=None, name=None):
    rows = []
    for bird in BIRDS:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        ci = None if ci_of is None else ci_of[bird]
        A = event_average(bird, times_of, ci)
        avg = A.mean(0)
        n_ev = len(A)
        for rd in readings:
            if rd == "a":
                level, lo, hi = uva.shuffle_band(inside_bout_pool(bird, ci), n_ev, PRE, POST, n_shuffle, rng)
            else:
                level, lo, hi = circ_shift_band(bird, times_of, n_shuffle, rng, ci)
            if name:
                AVG[(name, bird, rd)] = (avg, level, lo, hi)
            thr = hi if direction == "up" else lo
            t_ext, t_cross = uva.crossing_before(avg, LAGS, 0, thr, direction)
            rows.append({"bird": bird, "shuffle": rd, "events": n_ev, "extreme_ms": t_ext,
                         "leaves_band_ms": t_cross, "avg_level": level, "band_lo": lo, "band_hi": hi,
                         "extreme_value": avg[LAGS == t_ext][0]})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

fig4c-call-premotor¶

Uva activity rises sharply just before distance calls, leaving baseline 30 ms and peaking 15 ms before call onset.

Calls are the segments labelled "k" (b871 and Uva4; Orange150 has none). Calls occur outside song bouts, so the baseline windows are drawn from the call files themselves (random times in the call files) as well as from inside bouts, the claims file's reading; both are shown.

In [7]:
def call_events(bird):
    out = []
    for ev in uva.events(eph, bird):
        if any(ev["props"].get(p, False) for p in uva.OUTSIDE_FLAGS):
            continue
        k = ev["sel"] & (ev["title"] == "k")
        if k.sum():
            out.append((ev, eph["recs"][ev["key"]]["mua"][CI[bird]], ev["on"][k]))
    return out


rows = []
for bird in BIRDS:
    ce = call_events(bird)
    if not ce:
        rows.append({"bird": bird, "calls": 0}); continue
    A = np.concatenate([uva.aligned(m, t, PRE, POST)[0] for _, m, t in ce])
    avg = A.mean(0)
    for base in ["inside bouts (claims file)", "call files"]:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
        if base.startswith("inside"):
            level, lo, hi = uva.shuffle_band(inside_bout_pool(bird), len(A), PRE, POST, 1000, rng)
        else:
            pool = [(m, np.arange(PRE, len(m) - POST - 1)) for _, m, _ in ce]
            level, lo, hi = uva.shuffle_band(pool, len(A), PRE, POST, 1000, rng)
        t_pk, t_cross = uva.crossing_before(avg, LAGS, 0, hi, "up")
        if base.startswith("inside"):
            AVG[("calls", bird, "a")] = (avg, level, lo, hi)
        rows.append({"bird": bird, "calls": len(A), "baseline": base, "peak_ms": t_pk, "leaves_band_ms": t_cross,
                     "peak": avg[LAGS == t_pk][0], "band_hi": hi, "avg_level": level})
calls_tab = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(calls_tab.round(4).to_string(index=False))
for base in calls_tab.baseline.dropna().unique():
    s = calls_tab[calls_tab.baseline == base]
    crossed = s[s.leaves_band_ms.notna()].bird.tolist()
    print(f"{base}: latency of peak, mean over {s.peak_ms.notna().sum()} birds with calls, {-s.peak_ms.mean():.1f} ms "

    bird, day, f = ev["key"]

        return d[0] if d else None
    s = sheet[(sheet.bird == bird) & (sheet.day == day) & (sheet.file == f)]
    return f"{day} {s.depth.iloc[0]}" if len(s) and np.isfinite(s.depth.iloc[0]) else None

fig6-peak-before-onset and fig6-dip-before-offset¶

Uva activity rises significantly before syllable onsets in every bird, peaking 20 ms before onset and rising above its average level during singing 32 ms before onset.

Uva activity falls significantly before syllable offsets in every bird, reaching a minimum 18 ms before offset and dropping below its average level during singing 48 ms before offset.

Syllables are the selected song syllables (motif letters; introductory notes and calls are separate claims).

def paired_tests(win_of, ref, bird):
    """Per rendition: mean MUA in the window against the rendition's bout mean (a) or the
    reference window (b)."""
    x, ya, yb = [], [], []
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird):
        idx = np.where(syl_mask(ev))[0]
        for i in idx:
            w0, w1 = win_of(ev, i)
            if w0 < 0 or w1 > len(m):
                continue
            bt = [(a, b) for a, b, _ in ev["bouts"] if a <= ev["on"][i] <= b]
            r = ref(ev, i)
            if not bt or r is None or r[0] < 0 or r[1] > len(m):
                continue
            x.append(m[int(w0):int(w1)].mean())
            ya.append(m[int(bt[0][0]):int(bt[0][1])].mean())
            yb.append(m[int(r[0]):int(r[1])].mean())
    x, ya, yb = map(np.array, (x, ya, yb))
    ta, tb = stats.ttest_rel(x, ya), stats.ttest_rel(x, yb)
    return {"bird": bird, "n": len(x), "mean_window": x.mean(), "mean_bout": ya.mean(), "t_a": ta.statistic,
            "p_a": ta.pvalue, "mean_ref_b": yb.mean(), "t_b": tb.statistic, "p_b": tb.pvalue}


def prev_offset_window(ev, i):
    if i == 0:
        return None
    o = ev["off"][i - 1]
    return (o - 20, o + 20)

fig5-consistent-across-renditions and fig5-consistent-across-sites¶

Uva activity is consistent across renditions of the song motif; time-warped MUA is correlated across renditions (0.64 with 5 ms smoothing) and coherent below 12 Hz (mean coherence 0.68 between 1 and 12 Hz).

Uva activity is similar at different recording depths along a penetration; correlation 0.62 with 5 ms smoothing and mean coherence 0.65 between 1 and 12 Hz, with no evidence that activity varies across sites.

The motif of each bird is its most common sequence of motif letters (printed). A rendition is a run of consecutive segments spelling the motif, each selected. MUA is warped onto the template (the rendition whose length is closest to the median; Methods, Time warping), with the syllable onsets and offsets as alignment points. For the correlation the 2 ms MUA is smoothed further to a 5 ms total SD. Coherence uses one Slepian taper with time half-bandwidth 2 on the 2 ms MUA; the null is 1000 random circular shifts of each rendition (Rhythmicity).

In [12]:
from collections import Counter


def motif_of(bird):
    c = Counter()
    for ev in song_events(bird):
        s = "".join(t if (sel and t not in ("i", "k", "")) else "|" for t, sel in zip(ev["title"], ev["sel"]))
        for part in s.split("|"):
            letters = sorted(set(part))
            n = len(letters)
            for j in range(len(part) - n + 1):
                c[part[j:j + n]] += 1
    full = max((m for m in c if len(set(m)) == len(m)), key=lambda m: (len(m) >= 4, c[m] * len(m)))
    return full, c[full]


renditions = {}
for bird in BIRDS:
    motif, n = motif_of(bird)
    rows = []
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird):
        tt = list(ev["title"])
        for j in range(len(tt) - len(motif) + 1):
            if "".join(tt[j:j + len(motif)]) == motif and ev["sel"][j:j + len(motif)].all():
                pts = np.ravel(np.c_[ev["on"][j:j + len(motif)], ev["off"][j:j + len(motif)]])
                if np.all(np.diff(pts) > 0) and pts[0] >= 0 and pts[-1] < len(m):
                    rows.append((ev, m, pts))
    lens = np.array([p[-1] - p[0] for _, _, p in rows])
    tmpl = rows[int(np.argmin(np.abs(lens - np.median(lens))))][2]
    renditions[bird] = {"motif": motif, "rows": rows, "template": tmpl - tmpl[0], "lens": lens}
    print(f"{bird}: motif '{motif}', {len(rows)} renditions, length median {np.median(lens):.0f} ms "
          f"(range {lens.min():.0f} to {lens.max():.0f})")


def warped(bird, smooth_total_sd=None):
    R = renditions[bird]
    out = []
    for ev, m, pts in R["rows"]:
        x = m if smooth_total_sd is None else uva.gauss_smooth(m, np.sqrt(smooth_total_sd ** 2 - 2 ** 2))
        out.append(uva.warp(x, pts, R["template"]))
    return np.stack(out)


def corr_readings(W):
    Z = (W - W.mean(1, keepdims=True)) / W.std(1, keepdims=True)
    C = Z @ Z.T / W.shape[1]
    iu = np.triu_indices(len(W), 1)
    a = C[iu].mean()
    # (b) peak of the cross-correlation within +-50 ms, averaged over pairs (up to 300 pairs)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
    pairs = np.array(iu).T
    pairs = pairs[rng.choice(len(pairs), min(300, len(pairs)), replace=False)]
    L = W.shape[1]
    b = np.mean([max(np.corrcoef(Z[i][max(0, s):L + min(0, s)], Z[j][max(0, -s):L - max(0, s)])[0, 1]
                     for s in range(-50, 51, 2)) for i, j in pairs])
    c = np.mean([np.corrcoef(W[i], np.delete(W, i, 0).mean(0))[0, 1] for i in range(len(W))])
    return a, b, c


def coherence_readings(W, n_null=1000, seed=0):
    nfft = 2 ** int(np.ceil(np.log2(W.shape[1])) + 2)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(nfft, 1 / 1000)
    X = uva.mt_fft(W, nfft)
    band = (f >= 1) & (f <= 12)
    n = len(W)
    iu = np.triu_indices(n, 1)
    if len(iu[0]) > 2000:
        sel = np.random.default_rng(seed).choice(len(iu[0]), 2000, replace=False)
        iu = (iu[0][sel], iu[1][sel])
    Ca = np.abs(uva.coherency(X[iu[0]], X[iu[1]]))
    others = np.stack([np.delete(W, i, 0).mean(0) for i in range(n)])
    Cc = np.abs(uva.coherency(X, uva.mt_fft(others, nfft)))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    null = []
    for _ in range(n_null):
        Ws = np.stack([np.roll(w, rng.integers(len(w))) for w in W])
        Xs = uva.mt_fft(Ws, nfft)
        null.append(np.abs(uva.coherency(X[iu[0]], Xs[iu[1]]))[band].max())
    return Ca[band].mean(), Cc[band].mean(), np.percentile(null, 95), f, Ca

site_rows, site_pair_rows = [], []
for bird in BIRDS:
    R = renditions[bird]
    W5 = warped(bird, 5.0); W2 = warped(bird)
    sites = np.array([site_of(ev) for ev, _, _ in R["rows"]], dtype=object)
    days = np.array([ev["key"][1] for ev, _, _ in R["rows"]])
    names = [s for s in pd.unique(sites) if s is not None and np.sum(sites == s) >= 5]
    for s in names:
        site_rows.append({"bird": bird, "site": s, "renditions": int(np.sum(sites == s))})
    for i in range(len(names)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(names)):
            si, sj = sites == names[i], sites == names[j]
            if days[si][0] != days[sj][0]:
                continue  # sites of one penetration: same day
            r_avg = np.corrcoef(W5[si].mean(0), W5[sj].mean(0))[0, 1]
            Zi = (W5[si] - W5[si].mean(1, keepdims=True)) / W5[si].std(1, keepdims=True)
            Zj = (W5[sj] - W5[sj].mean(1, keepdims=True)) / W5[sj].std(1, keepdims=True)
            r_single = (Zi @ Zj.T / W5.shape[1]).mean()
            nfft = 2 ** int(np.ceil(np.log2(W2.shape[1])) + 2)
            f = np.fft.rfftfreq(nfft, 1 / 1000)
            Xi, Xj = uva.mt_fft(W2[si], nfft), uva.mt_fft(W2[sj], nfft)
            ii, jj = np.meshgrid(np.arange(si.sum()), np.arange(sj.sum()), indexing="ij")
            ii, jj = ii.ravel(), jj.ravel()
            if len(ii) > 2000:
                k = np.random.default_rng(3).choice(len(ii), 2000, replace=False); ii, jj = ii[k], jj[k]
            coh = np.abs(uva.coherency(Xi[ii], Xj[jj]))
            band = (f >= 1) & (f <= 12)
            site_pair_rows.append({"bird": bird, "site_1": names[i], "site_2": names[j], "corr_a_site_averages": r_avg,
                                   "corr_b_single_renditions": r_single, "coh_b_single_renditions_1_12": coh[band].mean()})

fig7a-correlation-with-amplitude, fig7b-10hz-power-peaks, fig7d-10hz-coherence¶

Uva activity correlates with song amplitude (peak correlation 0.40) and leads it by 42 ms.

Song amplitude and Uva activity both have a broad spectral peak near 10 Hz, at 8.0 Hz for song and 8.8 Hz for Uva.

Uva activity and song amplitude are significantly coherent near 10 Hz (peak at 8.8 Hz, coherence 0.75, p < 0.01, phase -0.77 pi), with a large peak in their cross-spectrum.

Segments are (a) bouts of 1 to 8.192 s (the shortest bout is not given; 1 s, a standard choice, so that the taper's 4 Hz resolution can show a 10 Hz peak) and (b) motif renditions (unwarped). The amplitude readings are (a) dB, (b) power without the log, (c) rectified audio smoothed at 2 ms. Spectra are padded to 8192 points at 1 kHz; longer bouts are left out (counted).

In [16]:
NFFT = 8192
FR = np.fft.rfftfreq(NFFT, 1 / 1000)
long_bouts = {}


def segments(bird, kind):
    out = []
    if kind == "bouts":
        for ev, m in bird_traces(bird):
            r = eph["recs"][ev["key"]]
            for a, b, _ in ev["bouts"]:
                a, b = int(a), int(b)
                if b - a > NFFT:
                    long_bouts[bird] = long_bouts.get(bird, 0) + 1
                    continue
                if b - a >= 1000 and b <= len(m):
                    out.append((m[a:b], r["amp_db"][a:b], 10 ** (r["amp_db"][a:b] / 10), r["amp_rect"][a:b]))
    else:
        for ev, m, pts in renditions[bird]["rows"]:
            r = eph["recs"][ev["key"]]
            a, b = int(pts[0]), int(pts[-1])
            out.append((m[a:b], r["amp_db"][a:b], 10 ** (r["amp_db"][a:b] / 10), r["amp_rect"][a:b]))
    return out


AMP = {"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3}
xc_rows = []
for bird in BIRDS:
    for kind in ["bouts", "motifs"]:
        segs = segments(bird, kind)
        for rd, j in AMP.items():
            lags = np.arange(-150, 151)
            cc = []
            for s in segs:
                x, y = s[0].astype(float), s[j].astype(float)
                vals = []
                for L in lags:  # positive lag: MUA earlier than amplitude
                    if L >= 0:
                        xx, yy = x[:len(x) - L], y[L:]
                    else:
                        xx, yy = x[-L:], y[:len(y) + L]
                    vals.append(np.corrcoef(xx, yy)[0, 1])
                cc.append(vals)
            cc = np.nanmean(cc, 0)
            k = int(np.argmax(np.abs(cc)))
            xc_rows.append({"bird": bird, "segments": kind, "amplitude": rd, "n": len(segs),
                            "peak_corr": cc[k], "lag_ms_mua_first": lags[k], "corr_at_0": cc[150]})
xc = pd.DataFrame(xc_rows)

spec_rows, coh_store = [], {}
for bird in BIRDS:
    for kind in ["bouts", "motifs"]:
        segs = segments(bird, kind)
        for rd, j in AMP.items():
            Xm = np.concatenate([uva.mt_fft(s[0].astype(float), NFFT) for s in segs])
            Xa = np.concatenate([uva.mt_fft(s[j].astype(float), NFFT) for s in segs])
            lens = np.array([len(s[0]) for s in segs], float)
            Pm = np.abs(Xm[:, 0]) ** 2; Pa = np.abs(Xa[:, 0]) ** 2
            coh_store[(bird, kind, rd)] = (Xm, Xa)
            for norm in ["sum", "length"]:
                if norm == "sum":
                    pm = (Pm / Pm.sum(1, keepdims=True)).mean(0); pa = (Pa / Pa.sum(1, keepdims=True)).mean(0)
                else:
                    pm = (Pm / lens[:, None]).mean(0); pa = (Pa / lens[:, None]).mean(0)
                spec_rows.append({"bird": bird, "segments": kind, "amplitude": rd, "norm": norm, "pm": pm, "pa": pa})
spec = pd.DataFrame(spec_rows)

Over motifs with the amplitude as power (reading b), the averaged coherency peaks at 9.0 Hz with coherence 0.789 and phase -0.721 pi, above the null of shifted MUA (p = 0.001, 1000 shifts; paper 8.8 Hz, 0.75, -0.77 pi, p < 0.01). spectral-features-weak¶

None of six spectral song features correlates significantly with Uva activity within a bird; pooled over birds only amplitude (r = 0.18) and gravity center (r = 0.17) do, after Bonferroni correction.

The six features are computed from the sound channel at 1 kHz after the Sound Analysis Pro definitions (uva.sap_features; the claims file adopts SAP as an assumption, and the details of the window, taper, band, AM and FM are standard choices stated in the helper). Windows run from 10 ms after each selected song syllable's onset to 10 ms before its offset, and the MUA window is the same window 42 ms earlier. Reading (a): per rendition, mean feature against mean MUA; reading (b): per 1 ms bin within the windows. Pearson r, Bonferroni over 6 features (p < 0.05/6). Pooled: all birds' renditions together, raw and (variant, reading a) with features and MUA z-scored within each bird's syllable type.

rows, pooled = [], {"a": [], "a_z": [], "b": []}
for bird in BIRDS:
    per_a, per_b = [], []
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird):
        F = eph["recs"][ev["key"]]["features"]
        for i in np.where(syl_mask(ev))[0]:
            a, z = int(ev["on"][i]) + 10, int(ev["off"][i]) - 10
            if z - a < 5 or a - 42 < 0 or z > len(m):
                continue
            mu = m[a - 42:z - 42]
            per_a.append([ev["title"][i], mu.mean()] + [F[f][a:z].mean() for f in uva.FEATURES])
            per_b.append(np.c_[mu, np.stack([F[f][a:z] for f in uva.FEATURES], 1)])
    A = pd.DataFrame(per_a, columns=["type", "mua"] + uva.FEATURES)
    B = np.concatenate(per_b)
    Az = A.copy()
    for col in ["mua"] + uva.FEATURES:
        Az[col] = A.groupby("type")[col].transform(lambda v: (v - v.mean()) / v.std() if v.std() > 0 else v * 0)
    pooled["a"].append(A); pooled["a_z"].append(Az.dropna()); pooled["b"].append(B)
    for j, f in enumerate(uva.FEATURES):
        ra = stats.pearsonr(A.mua, A[f]); rb = stats.pearsonr(B[:, 0], B[:, j + 1])
        rows.append({"bird": bird, "feature": f, "renditions": len(A), "r_a": ra.statistic, "p_a": ra.pvalue,
                     "sig_a": ra.pvalue < 0.05 / 6, "bins": len(B), "r_b": rb.statistic, "p_b": rb.pvalue,
                     "sig_b": rb.pvalue < 0.05 / 6})
sf = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Per bird:")
print(sf.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.3g}"))
prow = []
for rd in ["a", "a_z", "b"]:
    if rd == "b":
        X = np.concatenate(pooled["b"]); mua_, feats_ = X[:, 0], {f: X[:, j + 1] for j, f in enumerate(uva.FEATURES)}
    else:
        X = pd.concat(pooled[rd]); mua_, feats_ = X.mua.values, {f: X[f].values for f in uva.FEATURES}
    for f in uva.FEATURES:
        r = stats.pearsonr(mua_, feats_[f])
        prow.append({"reading": rd, "feature": f, "n": len(mua_), "r": r.statistic, "p": r.pvalue,
                     "significant_bonferroni": r.pvalue < 0.05 / 6})
print("\nPooled over birds:")
print(pd.DataFrame(prow).to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.3g}"))
print("\nFeatures significant in single birds, per reading:",
      {rd: int(sf[f"sig_{rd}"].sum()) for rd in ["a", "b"]}, "of", len(sf), "bird-feature pairs")
print("Paper: none significant in single birds; pooled, amplitude r = 0.18 and gravity center r = 0.17 significant, "
      "the other four not.")

Result: not reproduced (assumed feature definitions). Within single birds, 9 of 18 bird-feature pairs are significant per rendition (reading a) and 15 of 18 per 1 ms bin (reading b); the paper reports none. Pooled over birds, amplitude correlates with MUA (r = 0.156 per rendition, 0.183 per bin, the latter within 0.18 +- 0.018), but so do the other features: gravity center r = 0.291 (a) and 0.082 (b), outside 0.17 +- 0.017, and pitch goodness, Wiener entropy and FM are significant under readings (a) and (b). With each feature z-scored within syllable type, pitch goodness and FM stay significant and Wiener entropy does not (p = 0.06). The features follow SAP's definitions only as far as the helper states, but amplitude, the feature that depends least on them, alone breaks the single-bird condition. With hundreds to thousands of renditions per bird, correlations as small as 0.06 are significant; the paper does not give its n, so a difference in power may explain part of the disagreement.

fig9-long-syllable-gamma¶

In long syllables (> 150 ms; 13 syllables, 43% of song syllables) Uva activity can oscillate fast; 8 of 13 have a significant spectral peak above 10 Hz, at 17 to 51 Hz, and Uva activity is coherent with song amplitude from 1 to 55 Hz.

Syllable types (labels) of each bird whose median duration exceeds 150 ms. For each type, MUA and amplitude (reading a, dB) from onset to 50 ms before offset, spectra with [2 1] tapers padded to 1024 points, normalized by their sum and averaged over renditions. Null for the MUA spectrum: the 1 kHz MUA samples of each window scrambled and smoothed again with the 2 ms Gaussian, taking the scrambled window as periodic so that the smoothing adds no dip at its edges (the paper scrambles the raw signal; the reduced trace is scrambled here), 1000 times; a type has a significant peak when its largest local maximum above 10 Hz exceeds the 95th percentile of the null's maxima above 10 Hz. Coherence with amplitude is averaged over renditions per type, then over all long types, against the null of scrambled MUA averaged the same way (95th percentile of its maxima over 1 to 60 Hz, 200 draws).

In [22]:
NF9 = 1024
F9 = np.fft.rfftfreq(NF9, 1 / 1000)
hi = F9 > 10
band9 = (F9 >= 1) & (F9 <= 60)
rng = np.random.default_rng(9)
long_rows, coh9, null9 = [], [], []
n_types = 0
for bird in BIRDS:
    durs = {}
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird):
        for t, a, b, s in zip(ev["title"], ev["on"], ev["off"], ev["sel"]):
            if s and t not in ("i", "k", ""):
                durs.setdefault(t, []).append((ev, m, a, b))
    for t, items in sorted(durs.items()):
        if len(items) < 5:
            continue
        n_types += 1
        med = np.median([b - a for _, _, a, b in items])
        if med <= 150:
            continue
        segs = [(m[int(a):int(b) - 50].astype(float), eph["recs"][ev["key"]]["amp_db"][int(a):int(b) - 50].astype(float))
                for ev, m, a, b in items if b - a - 50 >= 50 and int(b) - 50 <= len(m)]
        Xm = np.concatenate([uva.mt_fft(x, NF9) for x, _ in segs])
        Xa = np.concatenate([uva.mt_fft(y, NF9) for _, y in segs])
        P = np.abs(Xm[:, 0]) ** 2
        P = (P / P.sum(1, keepdims=True)).mean(0)
        nullmax = []
        nc = []
        for it in range(1000):
            Xs = uva.scrambled_ffts([x for x, _ in segs], NF9, rng)
            Ps = np.abs(Xs[:, 0]) ** 2
            Ps = (Ps / Ps.sum(1, keepdims=True)).mean(0)
            nullmax.append(Ps[hi].max())
            if it < 200:
                nc.append(np.abs(uva.coherency(Xs, Xa)))
        thr = np.percentile(nullmax, 95)
        # the largest local maximum above 10 Hz (a peak, not the edge of the band)
        locmax = np.r_[False, (P[1:-1] > P[:-2]) & (P[1:-1] > P[2:]), False] & hi
        k = np.argmax(np.where(locmax, P, -np.inf)[hi])
        C = np.abs(uva.coherency(Xm, Xa))
        coh9.append(C); null9.append(np.array(nc))
        thr_t = np.percentile(np.array(nc)[:, band9].max(1), 95)
        ok_t = C > thr_t
        span = (F9 >= 1.1) & (F9 <= 49.5)
        long_rows.append({"bird": bird, "type": t, "median_ms": med, "renditions": len(segs),
                          "peak_above_10Hz": F9[hi][k], "peak_power": P[hi][k], "null95_max": thr,
                          "significant": bool(P[hi][k] > thr), "coh_null95": thr_t,
                          "coh_above_null_1.1_49.5Hz": f"{ok_t[span].mean():.2f}", "coh_unbroken_1.1_49.5Hz": bool(ok_t[span].all())})
lt = pd.DataFrame(long_rows)
print(lt.round(5).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nLong types: {len(lt)} of {n_types} syllable types with at least 5 renditions ({len(lt) / n_types:.2f}); "
      f"paper 13 (43%) over 5 birds")
sig = lt[lt.significant]
print(f"Long types with a significant peak above 10 Hz: {len(sig)} of {len(lt)} ({len(sig) / len(lt):.2f}); "
      f"peak frequencies {sorted(sig.peak_above_10Hz.round(1).tolist())}; paper 8 of 13 (0.62), 17 to 51 Hz")

thr_c = np.percentile(np.mean(null9, 0)[:, band9].max(1), 95)  # null of the across-type average, maxima over 1-60 Hz
above = Cm > thr_c

for fv, ab in zip(F9[band], above[band]):

if start is not None:

Result: not reproduced (assumed channel). Over 3 birds, 6 of 18 syllable types are longer than 150 ms (0.33; paper 0.43 +- 0.043). 5 of the 6 have a significant MUA peak above 10 Hz (0.83; paper 0.62 +- 0.062), at 10.7 to 40.0 Hz (lower bound outside 15.3 to 56.1 Hz). With the scrambled null smoothed without edge effects, the coherence with amplitude averaged over the long types exceeds its null (0.107) from 2.0 to 59.6 Hz without a break, covering 1.1 to 49.5 Hz; averaged within each bird and then over the 3 birds, as the criterion says, it exceeds its null (0.141) over the same range. The coherence part holds; the counts and the frequency range do not.

bout-offset-suppression¶

Uva activity is transiently suppressed for about 200 ms after bout offsets.

MUA aligned to bout offsets (the end of the last segment of each bout holding song syllables), against the shuffled baseline drawn at random times outside singing (more than 300 ms from any segment) in the same files, with the 95% band of the shuffles' minima over -100 to +500 ms.

In [23]:
rows = []
for bird in BIRDS:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(21)
    A, pool = [], []
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird):
        song = syl_mask(ev)
        offs = np.array([b for a, b, idx in ev["bouts"] if song[idx].any()])
        A.append(uva.aligned(m, offs, 100, 500)[0])
        alls = np.zeros(len(m), bool)
        for a, b in zip(ev["on"], ev["off"]):
            alls[max(0, int(a) - 300):int(b) + 300] = True
        t = np.where(~alls)[0]
        t = t[(t >= 100) & (t < len(m) - 501)]
        if len(t):
            pool.append((m, t))
    A = np.concatenate(A)
    avg = A.mean(0)
    lags = np.arange(-100, 501)
    level, lo, hi_ = uva.shuffle_band(pool, len(A), 100, 500, 1000, rng)
    AVG[("bout offsets", bird, "a")] = (avg, level, lo, hi_)
    below = avg < lo
    post = lags >= 0
    first = np.argmax(below & post) if np.any(below & post) else None
    if first is not None:
        j = first
        while j + 1 < len(avg) and avg[j + 1] < lo:
            j += 1
        end_below = lags[j]
        back = np.where((lags > lags[first]) & (avg >= lo))[0]
        dur_in = lags[back[0]] if len(back) else np.nan
        k = np.where((lags > lags[first]) & (avg >= level))[0]
        dur_level = lags[k[0]] if len(k) else np.nan
    else:
        end_below, dur_in, dur_level = np.nan, np.nan, np.nan
    rows.append({"bird": bird, "bout_offsets": len(A), "baseline_level": level, "band_lo": lo, "min_after": avg[post].min(),
                 "min_at_ms": lags[post][np.argmin(avg[post])], "first_below_ms": lags[first] if first is not None else np.nan,
                 "back_in_band_ms": dur_in, "back_to_level_ms": dur_level})
bo = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(bo.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print(f"Mean over birds: returns into the band {bo.back_in_band_ms.mean():.0f} ms after offset; "
      f"returns to the baseline level {bo.back_to_level_ms.mean():.0f} ms (paper about 200 ms, tolerance 180 to 220)")

The suppression is present; its duration is outside the tolerance and varies widely between birds.

no-motif-bout-signal¶

Uva shows little activation related to the onsets or offsets of motifs or bouts.

Per rendition, mean MUA in the 40 ms before onset (the window of the fig6 test) for motif onsets (first syllable of a motif rendition), bout onsets (the first song syllable of a bout, after any introductory notes) and other syllable onsets. One-sided two-sample t-test (motif or bout larger) at p < 0.05, the claims file's standard choice. After motif and bout offsets, the offset-aligned average is compared with the upper band of the shuffled baseline (inside bouts) from 0 to +150 ms.

In [25]:
rows = []
for bird in BIRDS:
    R = renditions[bird]
    motif_on = {}
    motif_off = {}
    for ev, m, pts in R["rows"]:
        motif_on.setdefault(ev["key"], []).append(pts[0]); motif_off.setdefault(ev["key"], []).append(pts[-1])
    v_motif, v_bout, v_other = [], [], []
    off_motif, off_bout = [], []
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird):
        song = syl_mask(ev)
        bout_first = set()
        for a, b, idx in ev["bouts"]:
            s = [i for i in idx if song[i]]
            if s:
                bout_first.add(s[0])
                off_bout.append(ev["off"][s[-1]])
        mo = set(np.round(motif_on.get(ev["key"], [])).astype(int))
        for i in np.where(song)[0]:
            t = int(round(ev["on"][i]))
            if t < 40:
                continue
            v = m[t - 40:t].mean()
            if t in mo:
                v_motif.append(v)
            elif i in bout_first:
                v_bout.append(v)
            else:
                v_other.append(v)
        off_motif += [(m, t) for t in motif_off.get(ev["key"], [])]
    tm = stats.ttest_ind(v_motif, v_other, alternative="greater")
    tb = stats.ttest_ind(v_bout, v_other, alternative="greater")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(31)
    exc = {}
    for name, items in [("motif offsets", off_motif)]:
        A = np.concatenate([uva.aligned(m, [t], PRE, POST)[0] for m, t in items])
        level, lo, hi_ = uva.shuffle_band(inside_bout_pool(bird), len(A), PRE, POST, 1000, rng)
        exc[name] = float((A.mean(0)[PRE:PRE + 151] - hi_).max())
    Ab = []
    for ev, m in bird_traces(bird):
        song = syl_mask(ev)
        offs = [ev["off"][[i for i in idx if song[i]][-1]] for a, b, idx in ev["bouts"] if any(song[i] for i in idx)]
        Ab.append(uva.aligned(m, offs, PRE, POST)[0])
    Ab = np.concatenate(Ab)
    level, lo, hi_ = uva.shuffle_band(inside_bout_pool(bird), len(Ab), PRE, POST, 1000, rng)
    exc["bout offsets"] = float((Ab.mean(0)[PRE:PRE + 151] - hi_).max())
    rows.append({"bird": bird, "n_motif_on": len(v_motif), "n_bout_on": len(v_bout), "n_other": len(v_other),
                 "motif_on": np.mean(v_motif), "bout_on": np.mean(v_bout), "other_on": np.mean(v_other),
                 "p_motif_gt_other": tm.pvalue, "p_bout_gt_other": tb.pvalue,
                 "max_excess_after_motif_off": exc["motif offsets"], "max_excess_after_bout_off": exc["bout offsets"]})
nm = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(nm.to_string(index=False))
print("A positive excess means the offset-aligned average rises above the band's upper edge after the offset.")

Result: not reproduced (assumed channel). MUA before motif onsets is significantly higher than before other syllable onsets in Orange150 (0.0635 against 0.0607, p = 0.0012), though not in b871 (p = 0.46) or Uva4 (p = 0.18). Bout onsets are not higher in any bird (p 0.78 to 0.99), and no average rises above the band after motif or bout offsets (largest excess below zero in all).

Lesion data¶

The lesion archive holds, for each of 7 birds, a folder of song before the lesion and one after it, each with the authors' analysis file (segment times at 44.1 kHz, and which segments are selected) and the .wav files it lists. The archive is streamed twice: first for the analysis files, then for the audio, of which only the amplitude traces and the bouts chosen for the maturity index are kept.

t0 = time.time()
les = uva.load_lesion_dbases()
print(f"Lesion analysis files read in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")


def syllables(db):
    """Selected segments per file (ms), sorted, and the file name."""
    out = []
    for f in db["files"]:
        s = f["seg"][f["selected"]] / db["fs"] * 1000.0
        if len(s):
            out.append((f["sound_file"], s[np.argsort(s[:, 0])]))
    return out

    T = np.array([f["time"] for f in db["files"]])
    syl = syllables(db)
    durs = np.concatenate([s[:, 1] - s[:, 0] for _, s in syl])
    days = pd.Series(pd.to_datetime(T - 719529, unit="D")).dt.date.value_counts().to_dict()
    summary.append({"bird": k[0], "condition": k[1], "fs": db["fs"], "files": len(db["files"]),
                    "segments": sum(len(f["seg"]) for f in db["files"]), "selected": len(durs),
                    "dates": {str(d): n for d, n in sorted(days.items())},
                    "span_h": (T.max() - T.min()) * 24, "audio_min": sum(f["length"] for f in db["files"]) / db["fs"] / 60,
                    "median_syl_ms": np.median(durs)})
summ = pd.DataFrame(summary)

SEED_MI = 1
rng_mi = np.random.default_rng(SEED_MI)
chosen, keep = {}, {}
for k in LKEYS:
    db = les["dbase"][k]
    fs = db["fs"]
    for gap in (300, 350):
        cands = []
        for f in db["files"]:
            s = f["seg"][f["selected"]]  # samples
            for b in uva.bouts_from_segments(s, gap / 1000 * fs):
                a, z = s[b, 0].min(), s[b, 1].max()
                if 0.7 * fs <= z - a <= 2 * fs:
                    cands.append((f["sound_file"], int(a), int(z)))
        pick = [cands[i] for i in sorted(rng_mi.choice(len(cands), min(100, len(cands)), replace=False))]
        chosen[(k, gap)] = (len(cands), pick)
        for w, a, z in pick:
            keep.setdefault((k[0], k[1], w), set()).add((a, z))
keep = {k: sorted(v) for k, v in keep.items()}

# Clock check: amplitude (dB) inside selected segments against outside, true and shifted labels.
rows = []
for k in LKEYS:
    db = les["dbase"][k]
    r = {"bird": k[0], "condition": k[1]}
    for shift in [0, 200, 1000]:
        ins, outs = [], []
        for w, s in syllables(db)[:300]:
            a = aud["amp"][(k[0], k[1], w)][0]
            mask = np.zeros(len(a), bool)
            for x, y in s + shift:
                mask[int(max(0, x)):int(min(len(a), y))] = True
            if mask.any() and (~mask).any():
                ins.append(a[mask].mean()); outs.append(a[~mask].mean())
        r[f"dB in minus out, shift {shift} ms"] = np.mean(ins) - np.mean(outs)
    rows.append(r)
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).round(2).to_string(index=False))

The analysis files hold one recording day before and one after the lesion for each bird (two post-lesion folders span two calendar dates, recordings that run past midnight). So the claims' readings of which post-lesion day to use (first day, or all days pooled) are the same here. The data do not say whether this post-lesion day is the first day of singing after surgery.

lesion-undirected-rate-similar¶

In social isolation, Uva-lesioned birds sing at rates similar to intact birds.

Recording hours are the span from the first to the last file of the day (the recordings are triggered by sound, so silent hours are not recorded; the span is the closest measure of time available). Rates per hour of span: syllables, bouts (gaps up to 300 ms) and singing time (bout durations), counted on the selected segments (the authors' song syllables) and, as a variant, on all segments. Rates per hour of recorded audio (summed file lengths) are shown too.

In [31]:
rows = []
for k in LKEYS:
    db = les["dbase"][k]
    T = np.array([f["time"] for f in db["files"]])
    span = (T.max() - T.min()) * 24
    syl = syllables(db)
    n_syl = sum(len(s) for _, s in syl)
    bouts = [(s[b, 0].min(), s[b, 1].max()) for _, s in syl for b in uva.bouts_from_segments(s, 300)]
    # all segments (selected or not), the authors' segmentation before their selection
    alls = [f["seg"][np.argsort(f["seg"][:, 0])] / db["fs"] * 1000.0 for f in db["files"] if len(f["seg"])]
    n_all = sum(len(s) for s in alls)
    bouts_all = [(s[b, 0].min(), s[b, 1].max()) for s in alls for b in uva.bouts_from_segments(s, 300)]
    audio_h = sum(f["length"] for f in db["files"]) / db["fs"] / 3600
    rows.append({"bird": k[0], "condition": k[1], "span_h": span, "audio_h": audio_h,
                 "selected_fraction": n_syl / n_all,
                 "syllables_per_h": n_syl / span, "bouts_per_h": len(bouts) / span,
                 "singing_s_per_h": sum(b - a for a, b in bouts) / 1000 / span,
                 "all_segments_per_h": n_all / span, "all_bouts_per_h": len(bouts_all) / span,
                 "all_singing_s_per_h": sum(b - a for a, b in bouts_all) / 1000 / span,
                 "all_segments_per_audio_h": n_all / audio_h, "syllables_per_audio_h": n_syl / audio_h,
                 "syllables": n_syl, "bouts": len(bouts), "all_segments": n_all, "all_bouts": len(bouts_all)})

Result: not reproduced (assumed measure). Counting the selected segments per hour of the recording span, lesioned birds sing less after the lesion: syllables per hour fall in 6 of 7 birds (post/pre ratio 0.08 to 1.01; Wilcoxon p = 0.031), as do bouts per hour (p = 0.047) and singing time (p = 0.031). The result depends on the count: with all segments, selected or not, the decreases are not significant (p = 0.078, 0.109 and 0.078), and the selected fraction differs between days (Purple53 0.59 before, 0.34 after). Per hour of recorded audio, all segments give p = 1.000 and selected segments p = 0.078, but recordings are triggered by sound, so recorded audio is not a measure of time. Spans range from 2.2 to 41.6 h.

fig2g-maturity-index-drop¶

Uva lesions lower the maturity index, a measure of song repeatability, from 0.26 to 0.08 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.025, 7 birds).

100 bouts of 0.7 to 2 s drawn at random (seed fixed) per bird and condition, for bout gaps of 300 and 350 ms. Spectrograms by the Methods' parameters, 860 Hz to 8.6 kHz. The claims file's readings (a) and (b) of the lag correlation function are run. The paper says "correlation of power spectra"; read literally (Pearson correlation of each pair of slices' power spectra), the silent and noisy slices of every bout correlate through the shared shape of the background spectrum. Whether the spectra are log-scaled and whether the mean spectrum is removed before correlating is not stated, and these change the outcome, so four forms are run: power or log power, each as is or with the mean over all slices of the bird's condition removed from each frequency (and divided by its SD). See the deviations for the reading adopted. The Methods cite Aronov et al. 2008 for this measure; its supplement could not be read in this run (HTTP 403).

In [32]:
mi_rows = []
t0 = time.time()
for k in LKEYS:
    for gap in (300, 350):
        n_c, pick = chosen[(k, gap)]
        specs = [uva.spectrogram_mt(aud["raw"][((k[0], k[1], w), a, z)].astype(float), 44100) for w, a, z in pick]
        for form in ["power", "log", "power centred", "log centred"]:
            S = [np.log(s + 1e-12) for s in specs] if form.startswith("log") else specs
            if form.endswith("centred"):
                allS = np.concatenate(S)
                mu, sd = allS.mean(0), allS.std(0)
                S = [(s - mu) / sd for s in S]
            a_, b_ = uva.maturity_index(S)
            mi_rows.append({"bird": k[0], "condition": k[1], "gap": gap, "form": form, "candidates": n_c,
                            "bouts": len(pick), "MI_a": a_, "MI_b": b_})
mi = pd.DataFrame(mi_rows)
print(f"(computed in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s)")
res = []
for (gap, form), g in mi.groupby(["gap", "form"]):
    for rd in ["MI_a", "MI_b"]:
        p = g.pivot(index="bird", columns="condition", values=rd)
        w = stats.wilcoxon(p["post-lesion"], p["pre-lesion"])
        res.append({"gap": gap, "form": form, "lag reading": rd[-1], "pre_mean": p["pre-lesion"].mean(),
                    "pre_sd": p["pre-lesion"].std(), "post_mean": p["post-lesion"].mean(), "post_sd": p["post-lesion"].std(),
                    "birds_decreasing": int((p["post-lesion"] < p["pre-lesion"]).sum()), "wilcoxon_p": w.pvalue,
                    "pre_in_tol": abs(p["pre-lesion"].mean() - 0.26) <= 0.03, "post_in_tol": abs(p["post-lesion"].mean() - 0.08) <= 0.02})
mi_res = pd.DataFrame(res)
print(mi_res.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nPer bird, log centred, gap 300 ms, reading a:")
print(mi[(mi.gap == 300) & (mi.form == "log centred")].pivot(index="bird", columns="condition", values="MI_a").round(3).to_string())
print("\nPer bird, power (literal reading), gap 300 ms, reading a:")
print(mi[(mi.gap == 300) & (mi.form == "power")].pivot(index="bird", columns="condition", values="MI_a").round(3).to_string())
print("Paper: pre 0.26 +- 0.03, post 0.08 +- 0.02, p < 0.025, 7 birds.")

Result: partially reproduced, resting on an assumption. With log spectra centred on the condition's mean spectrum, lag reading (a) and 300 ms gaps, MI falls from 0.235 to 0.096 (paper 0.26 +- 0.03 and 0.08 +- 0.02), in all 7 birds (Wilcoxon p = 0.016). That form is this attempt's, not a reading the claims file lists, and it is the only one of the 16 combinations that puts both values in tolerance (with 350 ms gaps the pre value is 0.213, just outside). Read literally (raw power or log power, not centred), MI does not fall (2 or fewer birds decrease) and its values (0.32 to 0.62) are far from the paper's. The Methods take the measure from Aronov et al. 2008, whose supplement could not be read in this run, so the decrease rests on the adopted form.

fig2f-closer-to-exponential¶

After Uva lesions syllable-duration distributions are much closer to exponential (goodness of fit Gamma 3.7 against 16 before; Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.025, 7 birds), but stay above the subsong criterion of Gamma < 2.

Syllables are the selected segments of each day. Gamma readings (a) D times the square root of n and (b) D over the Lilliefors critical value at alpha 0.05 (1.06 / sqrt(n) for the exponential, Lilliefors 1969). Ref 41 (Aronov et al. 2008) could not be read in this run (its supplement returned HTTP 403), so its definition could not be checked. Variant: the durations of SyllGaps.mat (one bird).

fig2c-small-syllable-peak¶

In 6 of 7 Uva-lesioned birds the post-lesion syllable-duration distribution has a small peak at 50 to 100 ms.

In [34]:
rows = []
for k in [k for k in LKEYS if k[1] == "post-lesion"]:
    durs = np.concatenate([s[:, 1] - s[:, 0] for _, s in syllables(les["dbase"][k])])
    for bw in (5, 10):
        edges = np.arange(0, 1000 + bw, bw)
        h, _ = np.histogram(durs, edges)
        c = edges[:-1] + bw / 2
        expd = len(durs) * (np.exp(-edges[:-1] / durs.mean()) - np.exp(-edges[1:] / durs.mean()))
        w = (c >= 50) & (c <= 100)
        loc = np.r_[False, (h[1:-1] > h[:-2]) & (h[1:-1] >= h[2:]), False]
        a_ = bool(np.any(loc & w & (h > expd)))
        hi95 = stats.poisson.ppf(0.975, expd)
        b_ = bool(np.any(loc & w & (h > hi95)))
        rows.append({"bird": k[0], "bin_ms": bw, "n": len(durs), "local_max_50_100_ms": c[loc & w].tolist(),
                     "reading_a": a_, "reading_b": b_})
pk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(pk.to_string(index=False))
for bw in (5, 10):

    print(f"bins {bw} ms: reading (a) {s.reading_a.sum()} of 7, reading (b) {s.reading_b.sum()} of 7 (paper 6 of 7)")

With 5 ms bins all 7 birds have a local maximum at 50 to 100 ms above the fitted exponential and above its 97.5% Poisson bound (both readings); with 10 ms bins (variant) 6 of 7 do, as the paper reports. The count under the main bins is 7, one more than the paper's 6. The histograms show that several of these maxima are bumps of one or two bins (LPink15 has four between 50 and 100 ms), so the 5 ms count is sensitive to count noise.

fig2d-gaps-broader¶

After Uva lesions gap durations become broadly distributed, with more long and more short gaps, like subsong.

In [36]:
rows = []
for b in LBIRDS:
    g = {}
    for cond in ["pre-lesion", "post-lesion"]:
        gs = []
        for _, s in syllables(les["dbase"][(b, cond)]):
            d = s[1:, 0] - s[:-1, 1]
            gs.append(d[d <= 300])
        g[cond] = np.concatenate(gs)
    lo, hi5 = np.percentile(g["pre-lesion"], [5, 95])
    post = g["post-lesion"]
    iqr = lambda x: np.subtract(*np.percentile(np.log(x[x > 0]), [75, 25]))
    rows.append({"bird": b, "gaps_pre": len(g["pre-lesion"]), "gaps_post": len(post), "pre_p5_ms": lo, "pre_p95_ms": hi5,
                 "post_frac_short": np.mean(post < lo), "post_frac_long": np.mean(post > hi5),
                 "post_frac_outside": np.mean((post < lo) | (post > hi5)),
                 "iqr_log_pre": iqr(g["pre-lesion"]), "iqr_log_post": iqr(post)})
gp = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(gp.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(f"Reading (a): birds with more than 10% outside {(gp.post_frac_outside > 0.10).sum()} of 7; both short and long fractions "
      f"above 5%: {((gp.post_frac_short > 0.05) & (gp.post_frac_long > 0.05)).sum()} of 7")
w = stats.wilcoxon(gp.post_frac_outside - 0.10)
print(f"   Wilcoxon on (fraction outside - 0.10): p = {w.pvalue:.4f}")

print(f"Reading (b): IQR of log gap larger after in {(gp.iqr_log_post > gp.iqr_log_pre).sum()} of 7; Wilcoxon p = {w2.pvalue:.4f}")

Result: reproduced. After the lesion 16 to 38% of gaps fall outside the bird's pre-lesion 5th to 95th percentiles, against 10% if unchanged (Wilcoxon p = 0.016); the long fraction rises in all 7 birds and the short fraction exceeds 5% in 6 of 7. The interquartile range of log gap widens in 5 of 7 birds (p = 0.078).

fig2e-rhythmicity-drop and fig2e-residual-rhythm-peak¶

Uva lesions decrease song rhythmicity, R, from 3.30 to 1.7 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.025, 7 birds).

Unlike subsong, 6 of 7 Uva-lesioned birds keep a significant peak in the song rhythm spectrum between 3 and 8 Hz.

Bouts with gaps of at most 350 ms and at least 1 s long (the shortest bout is not given; a standard choice). Amplitude readings (a) dB and (c) the log of the rectified, 2 ms smoothed audio (the Song rhythmicity section log-scales the amplitude, so reading (b), without the log, is not run for R). Null readings (a) the condition's own syllable and gap distributions, (b) the post-lesion distributions; synthetic bouts match each real bout's length; levels are the mean amplitude inside and outside syllables. R is the maximum of the ratio between 3 and 30 Hz (the upper bound is not given; a standard choice). The peak test draws 1000 synthetic bout sets, as the claims file asks. For post-lesion song the two null readings are the same, so the peak test is run once. A maximum of the ratio at the band's edge is not a peak, so the test is also run requiring a local maximum inside the band, and, as a variant, on the peak's prominence.

def rhythm_inputs(k, minlen=1000):
    db = les["dbase"][k]
    B, durs, gaps = [], [], []
    for w, s in syllables(db):
        durs += list(s[:, 1] - s[:, 0])
        d = s[1:, 0] - s[:-1, 1]
        gaps += list(d[d <= 350])
        dbt, rect = aud["amp"][(k[0], k[1], w)]
        for b in uva.bouts_from_segments(s, 350):
            a, z = int(s[b, 0].min()), int(s[b, 1].max())
            if z - a >= minlen and z <= len(dbt) and z - a <= uva.NFFT_RHYTHM:
                inside = np.zeros(z - a, bool)
                for x, y in s[b] - a:
                    inside[int(x):int(y)] = True
                B.append({"a": dbt[a:z].astype(float), "c": np.log(rect[a:z].astype(float) + 1e-9), "inside": inside})
    gaps = np.array(gaps)
    return B, np.array(durs), gaps[gaps > 0]


FRH = np.fft.rfftfreq(uva.NFFT_RHYTHM, 1 / 1000)
N_PEAK_DRAWS = 1000  # the claims file's number of null draws
peak_store = {}
rh_in = {k: rhythm_inputs(k) for k in LKEYS}
rh_rows, peak_rows = [], []
for k in LKEYS:
    B, durs, gaps = rh_in[k]
    for amp in ["a", "c"]:
        spec = np.mean([uva.bout_spectrum(b[amp]) for b in B], 0)
        lev_s = np.mean([b[amp][b["inside"]].mean() for b in B])
        lev_g = np.mean([b[amp][~b["inside"]].mean() for b in B if (~b["inside"]).any()])
        for null in ["a", "b"]:
            src = k if null == "a" else (k[0], "post-lesion")
            d_, g_ = rh_in[src][1], rh_in[src][2]
            rng = np.random.default_rng([LKEYS.index(k), ord(amp), ord(null)])
            lg = np.log(g_)

            def draw():
                return np.mean([uva.bout_spectrum(uva.synthetic_bout(len(b[amp]), d_.mean(), lg.mean(), lg.std(),
                                                                     lev_s, lev_g, rng)) for b in B], 0)
            nullspec = np.mean([draw() for _ in range(5)], 0)
            ratio = spec / nullspec
            m = (FRH > 3) & (FRH <= 30)
            rh_rows.append({"bird": k[0], "condition": k[1], "amplitude": amp, "null": null, "bouts": len(B),
                            "R": ratio[m].max(), "R_freq": FRH[m][np.argmax(ratio[m])],
                            "R_3_50": ratio[(FRH > 3) & (FRH <= 50)].max()})
            if k[1] == "post-lesion" and amp == "a" and null == "a":
                rr = []
                for _ in range(N_PEAK_DRAWS):
                    rr.append(draw() / nullspec)
                rr = np.array(rr)
                peak_store[k[0]] = (ratio, rr)
                for lo_, hi_ in [(3, 8), (4, 8)]:
                    bm = (FRH >= lo_) & (FRH <= hi_)
                    thr_max = np.percentile(rr[:, bm].max(1), 95)
                    thr_f = np.percentile(rr[:, bm], 95, axis=0)
                    peak_rows.append({"bird": k[0], "null": null, "band": f"{lo_}-{hi_} Hz", "max_ratio": ratio[bm].max(),
                                      "at_Hz": FRH[bm][np.argmax(ratio[bm])], "null95_of_max": thr_max,
                                      "significant_max": bool(ratio[bm].max() > thr_max),
                                      "significant_any_freq": bool(np.any(ratio[bm] > thr_f))})
rh = pd.DataFrame(rh_rows)

With the dB amplitude, R falls in all 7 birds (Wilcoxon p = 0.016 under both nulls), but the values are higher than the paper's: 4.84 before and 2.44 after with null (a) (paper 3.30 +- 1.1 and 1.7 +- 0.3), and 5.87 and 2.41 with null (b). def band_peak(r, bm):
    """Largest local maximum of the ratio strictly inside the band (higher than both neighbours,
    so not the band's edge), and its prominence within the band: its height above the higher
    of the lowest points on either side of it in the band. (nan, 0) when there is none."""
    idx = np.where(bm)[0]
    best, prom = np.nan, 0.0
    for j in idx[1:-1]:
        if r[j] > r[j - 1] and r[j] > r[j + 1] and not (r[j] <= best):
            best = r[j]
            prom = r[j] - max(r[idx[0]:j + 1].min(), r[j:idx[-1] + 1].min())
    return best, prom

Result: not reproduced. No version of the test gives the paper's 6 of 7. Taking the maximum of the ratio anywhere in the band, all 7 birds pass, but in 3 of them (Purple94, LPink13, LPink15) that maximum is the band's lower edge, 3.17 Hz. Requiring a local maximum inside the band, all 7 still pass (local maxima 1.29 to 3.34 against null thresholds of about 1.1 to 1.3, 1000 draws): the synthetic null has no amplitude texture within syllables, so the whole real ratio lies above it. Requiring the peak's prominence to exceed the null's prominences, 4 of 7 pass (5 of 7 between 4 and 8 Hz).

Blocked claims¶

  • lesion-directed-song-abolished: the paper and the data descriptor say directed song was recorded, but neither the file names (bird, date number, date and time; printed in the lesion data check), the analysis files (no properties) nor the descriptor mark any recording as directed. If directed recordings are in the folders, they cannot be told apart. Blocked, metadata insufficient.
  • figs1-control-lesions-no-effect: the archive holds 7 lesioned birds, the paper's Uva lesion count; there are no control-lesion birds. Blocked, data missing.
  • single-unit-spontaneous-rates: the analysis files hold no spike times (EventTimes empty) and no sorted units; the spreadsheets mark 32 "spontaneous activity" recordings, which are raw multiunit signals with no unit identities and nothing to say which units project to HVC. Blocked, metadata insufficient.
  • fig3-antidromic: the stimulation files are described in the cell below. Stimulus times can be taken from the artefacts, which come back to within 0.25 V of baseline a median 2.3 ms after their onset (1.3 to 8.7 ms over 40 files), inside the claim's 1.5 to 5 ms window; 36 of 779 stimuli have recovered before 1.5 ms. The claim's latency and jitter are those of identified single units, measured from stimulus times. The files hold no stimulus times and no sorted or identified units, and in a multiunit trace a response locked to the stimulus with under 100 us of jitter repeats on every trial like the artefact, so it cannot be told apart from it without the units and collision tests. The claim is not tested. Blocked, other. An earlier version of the cell counted spikes after subtracting each file's median trace; that removes any response locked to the stimulus, so the count was dropped.
  • fig8-no-gte-relation: needs GTE times from the model-based method of Boari et al. (ref 50). The paper links no code. A third-party copy of GTE extraction code from the Mindlin lab exists (github.com/kylerbrown/mindlin_auto); it is not the paper's implementation, was not tried here, and whether it runs is not known. Blocked, other (not attempted).

rows = []
for _, r in sheet[sheet.note.str.contains("stim")].iterrows():
    key = (r.bird, r.day, int(r.file))
    if key not in eph["recs"] or CHAN[r.bird] not in eph["recs"][key]["stim"]:
        continue
    sn, on = eph["recs"][key]["stim"][CHAN[r.bird]]
    t = (np.arange(sn.shape[1]) - 200) / 40.0  # ms from the artefact's first saturated sample
    base = np.median(sn[:, :180], axis=1, keepdims=True)
    dev = np.abs(sn - base) > 0.25  # V; the baseline's spread is about 0.05 V
    rec = np.array([t[np.where(d & (t <= 10))[0][-1]] if d.any() else np.nan for d in dev])
    w = (t >= 1.5) & (t <= 5)
    rows.append({"bird": r.bird, "day": r.day, "file": int(r.file), "note": r.note, "stimuli": len(sn),
                 "recovery_ms_median": np.nanmedian(rec), "recovered_before_1.5ms": int((rec < 1.5).sum()),
                 "frac_1.5_5ms_beyond_0.25V": dev[:, w].mean()})
art = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(art.round(2).to_string(index=False))
print(f"\nStimulation files with artefacts on the chosen channel: {len(art)}; median recovery to within 0.25 V of "
      f"baseline {art.recovery_ms_median.median():.1f} ms (range {art.recovery_ms_median.min():.1f} to "
      f"{art.recovery_ms_median.max():.1f}); fraction of the 1.5 to 5 ms window beyond 0.25 V, median "
      f"{art['frac_1.5_5ms_beyond_0.25V'].median():.2f}")
print(f"Stimuli whose artefact is back within 0.25 V before 1.5 ms: {art['recovered_before_1.5ms'].sum()} of {art.stimuli.sum()}")
print("Intensities in the spreadsheet notes:", sorted(set(art.note.str.extract(r"(\d+)\s*uA")[0].dropna())))
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(16, 3), sharey=True)
for ax, (_, r) in zip(axs, art.iloc[np.linspace(0, len(art) - 1, 4).astype(int)].iterrows()):
    sn, _ = eph["recs"][(r.bird, r.day, r.file)]["stim"][CHAN[r.bird]]
    t = (np.arange(sn.shape[1]) - 200) / 40.0
    ax.plot(t, sn.T, lw=0.4); ax.axvspan(1.5, 5, color="C1", alpha=0.15)
    ax.set_xlim(-1, 10); ax.set_ylim(-1, 1); ax.set_title(f"{r.bird} {r.day} file {r.file}", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlabel("ms from artefact onset")
axs[0].set_ylabel("V (clipped to +-1)")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("The traces saturate at +-10 V; the axes show +-1 V, so the saturated part lies outside them.")

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The electrophysiology covers 3 of the paper's 5 birds. Each recording has three neural channels and nothing in the files settles which is the Uva electrode; the channel with the largest syllable-onset modulation is used for each bird (an assumption that every electrophysiology outcome rests on; for Orange150 it is the channel the authors' analysis file ran its event detectors on). MUA is computed from the raw signal as the Methods say, then sampled at 1 kHz. Several methods the paper leaves open were run under each reading the claims file lists; the maturity index needed a form the claims file does not list (log spectra centred on the mean spectrum), adopted as an assumption because the literal reading cannot give values near the paper's. The song features follow Sound Analysis Pro's definitions as far as the helper states. The rhythm null and the shuffled baselines are built as the claims file describes; the synthetic rhythm null has no amplitude texture within syllables.

What was found about the data set. The lesion data match their analysis files exactly (12,833 wav files, all listed, all lengths equal). The electrophysiology archive holds a second copy of one recording day as a nested archive (173 identical files). The descriptor says introductory notes and calls are unselected, but they are selected and labelled "i" and "k"; it does not say which of the three neural channels is the recording electrode, nor what the labels mean. No lesion recording is marked as directed or undirected. One Uva4 recording (file 20) has an unreadable closing sample count. Two vector clustering files that the descriptor does not mention have the same size in two birds' folders. The spreadsheet tab for Uva4 is named "October 6, 2016" and lists dates from 2007-07-25 to 2007-07-27, while the analysis file runs to 2007-08-06.
